title: Report accepted VCF Installer bootstrap changes when depot sync fails
prompt:
Infrastructure automation ticket. Our VCF 9.1 bootstrap job configures the outbound proxy, saves the online depot credentials, and then starts a depot metadata sync. Today it reports the whole run as simply failed when the sync call errors, hiding the fact that the first two mutations were already accepted by VCF Installer. Implement the missing stdlib-only `vcf_installer` Python package so callers get an exact partial-progress report and can decide what is safe to retry.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a reduced contract derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Its provenance, pinned commit SHA, spec path, and every operationId are recorded in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. Use those fixtures as the source of truth; do not replace them with a documentation-page interpretation. The acceptance test starts a loopback-only mock which exposes only the three named operations and records every request. No live VMware endpoint or network access is needed.

Expose these public names from `vcf_installer`: `InstallerClient`, `ProxyConfiguration`, `DepotSettings`, `StepResult`, `ChangeReport`, `VCFInstallerAPIError`, and `configure_depot_access`. `InstallerClient(base_url, *, timeout=10.0)` must implement the three contract operations using only the Python standard library. JSON bodies use UTF-8 `application/json`; requests accept JSON. Treat only the operation's pinned success status as success. Its public `update_proxy_configuration` method returns `(status, decoded_response)`. Decode an error response into `VCFInstallerAPIError` with `.operation_id`, `.status`, `.error` (the complete decoded error object), and `.completed`. Its string form must include the server's error code and message.

The value-object constructor fields are `ProxyConfiguration(is_enabled, host=None, port=None, transfer_protocol=None, username=None, password=None, is_authenticated=None)` and `DepotSettings(download_activation_code=None, download_token=None, username=None, password=None, offline_username=None, offline_password=None, is_offline_depot=False, hostname=None, port=None, url=None)`. Serialize them to the exact camelCase schemas in the contract. Optional values that the caller did not set must be absent from the JSON object at every nesting level—not `null`, `""`, or empty placeholder objects. Explicit `False` remains meaningful and must be sent. Never send response-only fields. Do not add required-field or cross-field validation that is absent from the reduced contract: `DepotSettings()` is valid and serializes with only `depotConfiguration.isOfflineDepot`, without empty account objects.

`configure_depot_access(client, proxy, depot)` must call `updateProxyConfiguration`, then `updateDepotSettings`, then `syncDepotMetadata`, in that order. Record each accepted response as a `StepResult(operation_id, http_status, response)` without relabeling HTTP 202 as completed work. On success return a `ChangeReport` whose immutable `.steps` tuple contains all three results. On the first API error, stop immediately and re-raise it with `.completed` set to an immutable tuple of the exact earlier `StepResult` objects, in order; the failed operation must not appear there. Do not roll back or replay accepted steps.

The protected verifier checks method, path, query, headers, byte-for-byte compact JSON, empty-body behavior for the sync PATCH, omission of every unset optional field, error preservation, and accurate partial progress. Do not modify `tests/` or `docs/`. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v tests.test_depot_bootstrap` from the repository root.
